guide.title: Understand the task

scenarios.title: Retire two tools with different retention policies
scenarios.summary: Remove one program but keep its settings, purge another, and preserve dependent working tools.
scenarios.objective: Retire museum-report 1.0-1 but retain its customized /etc/museum/report.conf and configuration-only package record. Completely purge museum-retired, including its record, program and configuration. Keep museum-lib, museum-viewer, their files and /work/note.txt unchanged, all remaining dependencies satisfied, and the old cached list intact.

guide.title: Understand the task
guide.why: Retirement is not always deletion of everything. Remove keeps declared configuration files when present, leaving a configuration-only record; purge also removes those configuration files and the package record. A dependent working program may still need a shared library.

guide.title: Make targeted changes
guide.why: dpkg -r NAME removes a supplied package while retaining its conffiles. dpkg -P NAME purges it. Inspect status with dpkg-query -W -f='${Package} ${db:Status-Status}\n' NAME. These ${...} names are query-format fields, not shell variables. Read config-files as “program removed; configuration retained.” Do not remove a shared library still required by a preserved tool.
